genZNote: Catalase negative and technically an anaerobe, but chill enough with oxygen to headline your yogurt label.

morphology.shape: Long, slender rod (bacillus), sometimes slightly curved
morphology.oxygenRequirement: Aerotolerant anaerobe (often grouped with facultative anaerobes for growth purposes); grows best microaerophilically

habitat.naturalHabitat: Human and animal gastrointestinal tract, oral cavity, and vagina
habitat.hostAssociation: Normal commensal flora; a dominant organism of a healthy vaginal microbiome
habitat.environmentalOccurrence: Also found in fermented foods (yogurt, some cheeses) as a starter/probiotic culture

microscopy.appearance: Gram-positive rods, often long and slender

culture.media: MRS (de Man, Rogosa and Sharpe) agar or broth
culture.growthCharacteristics: Grows best at 37°C under reduced-oxygen/microaerophilic to anaerobic conditions; does not tolerate strict aerobic culture well despite being called 'aerotolerant'
culture.colonyMorphology: Small, white to gray, convex colonies

identificationClues: Gram-positive, catalase-negative rod (helps separate it from catalase-positive Bacillus/Corynebacterium)
Long, slender bacillus, often in chains
Normal dominant flora of the healthy vagina — maintains acidic pH via lactic acid production
Grows on MRS agar under microaerophilic/anaerobic conditions

diseases: Rarely pathogenic — opportunistic bacteremia or endocarditis reported almost exclusively in severely immunocompromised or critically ill patients
virulenceFactors: None of clinical significance — considered a low-virulence commensal/probiotic organism
clinicalImportance.transmission: Endogenous normal flora; not typically transmitted as a pathogen
clinicalImportance.epidemiology: Widely used commercially as a probiotic in yogurt and dietary supplements; maintenance of an acidic vaginal pH by lactic-acid-producing Lactobacillus species is thought to help protect against overgrowth of other organisms
clinicalImportance.labSignificance: Catalase-negative Gram-positive rods recovered from blood or sterile sites should not be dismissed automatically as a contaminant in the right clinical context, though this remains rare

examFacts.importantDisease: Rarely pathogenic — normal vaginal/gut flora and probiotic organism
examFacts.distinguishingFeature: Catalase-negative Gram-positive rod that dominates the healthy vaginal microbiome (Doderlein's bacillus)
